meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стучаться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to knock', forming an aspectual pair with 'стучаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Извините, ради бога! Я хотел постучаться и не рассчитал.
examples.trans: Forgive me, for goodness' sake! I wanted to knock and misjudged it.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'чить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to learn', forming an aspectual pair with 'выучить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to teach') (+ accusative of the person) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвонить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (a bell or phone) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('machine') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'concept, idea, notion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.
Max, I have no idea at all.

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'so'.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

надоесть.gloss: to bore, to get on someone's nerves

meanings.note: the person who is fed up is in the dative: 'мне надоело' = I'm fed up
Secondary conversational sense ('' + infinitive' = I'm tired of doing ...') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Надоело мне в этом архиве сидеть.
examples.trans: I'm tired of sitting in this archive.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
+ accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('five') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job
Secondary conversational sense ('post, position') (на его место = in his place) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'являть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to declare'.

examples.trans: Will you report to the police?

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'theft', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Полиция быстро задержала преступников за дерзкий угон дорогой машины.
examples.trans: The police quickly detained the criminals for the brazen theft of an expensive car.

examples.text: Владелец сразу заявил в полицию про ночной угон своего автомобиля.
examples.trans: The owner immediately reported the nighttime theft of his car to the police.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in front of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('before (in time)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('that') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: 'mum will kill me' = I'll be in big trouble

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to answer', forming an aspectual pair with 'отвечать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to answer the phone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Прости, я должен ответить. Да, Аллочка!
examples.trans: Sorry, I have to answer this. Yes, Allochka!

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

увезти.gloss: to take away (by vehicle), drive away

meanings.en: to take away, drive someone/something away
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'везти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to take away', forming an aspectual pair with 'увозить'.

examples.trans: We need to take him away somewhere.
They were driven out to the dacha.
We need to take him away somewhere, do you understand?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out', forming an aspectual pair with 'получаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: + past tense: 'чтобы свидетели были'
Secondary conversational sense ('in order to') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.
Secondary conversational sense ('in general') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.en: to acquire, start, get (a pet, friend, suitor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'вести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to acquire', forming an aspectual pair with 'заводить'.

examples.text: А сейчас ты завела себе молодого кавалера!
examples.trans: And now you got yourself a young suitor!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to open', forming an aspectual pair with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'mirror', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, у вас тут зеркало сломанное.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, you have a broken mirror here.
He smashes the mirror on her car.

починить.gloss: to fix, to repair, to mend

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чинить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fix', forming an aspectual pair with 'чинить'.

examples.trans: I will try to fix it myself.
